messages.content: Create a mix track using notes of C major scale and duration of each note being quarter of a second with a duration of 3 minutes.

function.name: music_composer_create_mix
function.description: Create a mix of a song based on a particular music scale and duration Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

scale.description: The musical scale to be used. E.g: C Major, A Minor, etc.

track_length.description: Length of the mix track in seconds.

message.reasoning: The user wants to create a mix track using notes of C major scale, each note duration being quarter of a second (i.e., 0.25 seconds). The track length is 3 minutes. 3 minutes = 180 seconds. Each note is 0.25 seconds, so number of notes = 180 / 0.25 = 720 notes. They want to use the function music_composer_create_mix. The function signature: scale: string, note_duration: "whole" | "half" | "quarter" | "eighth" | "sixteenth", track_length: number. But note_duration is one of those strings, not a numeric value. The user says "duration of each note being quarter of a second". That is not one of the options. The options are whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth. Quarter note is typically 1 beat, but we need to interpret. The user might mean quarter note duration. But they also say quarter of a second. That is ambiguous. We can interpret "quarter of a second" as quarter note? But quarter note is not a time unit. The function expects a note duration type. So we should choose "quarter" as the note duration. The track length is 180 seconds. So we call the function with scale="C Major", note_duration="quarter", track_length=180.
